item.title: Random log outs, amd_pstate failed to load, keyring mismatch, and more!
item.dc:creator: @arraybolt3
item.description:
sublime.dust:

It said to ensure that there are no nvidia drivers installed. When I checked for nvidia packages, I found that firmware-nvidia-graphics was installed.

Slight misunderstanding: the page says to ensure the proprietary NVIDIA driver is not installed. There are two NVIDIA drivers: Nouveau, an open-source driver that comes with Kicksecure, and the otherwise-unnamed proprietary NVIDIA driver. You want to keep Nouveau present, and ensure that no proprietary NVIDIA driver package (like nvidia-driver or cuda-driver) is installed.

firmware-nvidia-graphics is not actually a driver. Drivers consist of code that runs as part of the OS itself, while firmware typically runs on a processor built into the hardware it makes work. In this case, firmware-nvidia-graphics contains code that runs on the NVIDIA GPU itself, outside of the operating system. Both Nouveau and the proprietary NVIDIA driver require firmware, so it makes sense that removing it caused a black screen. It should remain installed.

If you haven’t installed the proprietary NVIDIA driver, you can ignore step 1 of the software rendering steps and just do the remaining steps.

item.title: Random log outs, amd_pstate failed to load, keyring mismatch, and more!
item.dc:creator: @arraybolt3
item.description:
sublime.dust:
  1. Logged out of computer at random intervals
    …
  2. systemd critical journal messages - nouveau, channel 16 killed

These are almost certainly related. Some solutions are documented here:

Kicksecure – 19 Sep 26

Sudden logout - NVIDIA

Because Nouveau runs by default in Kicksecure (the Debian default), issues may occur at any time. A recent example is a sudden black login screen caused by Nouveau GSP crashing and terminating labwc, which is used in lxqt-wayland [12]. | NVIDIA -...

sublime.dust:
  1. Kanshi config is not automatically applied upon startup

Did you place your configuration file at ~/.config/kanshi/config? That file must exist and not be empty for Kanshi to turn on at login. It might be turning on too early though, at least in theory. You can place the systemctl --user restart kanshi command in ~/.config/labwc/autostart to get it to run when the graphical session starts.

sublime.dust:
  1. amd_pstate failed to load

If the system is otherwise functional, you can probably ignore this. The missing module is to be expected, because amd_pstate is built into the core kernel binary in Debian (and by extension in Kicksecure, since we use Debian’s kernel).

sublime.dust:
  1. sudo apt update: Error due to keyring mismatch

Did you install Mullvad Browser using browser-choice, and then try to follow the instructions to install Mullvad VPN? That could cause a conflict, since browser-choice enables Mullvad’s repository, and following the VPN instructions thereafter will attempt to add the repository a second time. Since you’ve deleted both files that might hold the Mullvad repo keys, the easiest solution is probably to:

  1. Delete /etc/apt/sources.list.d/mullvad.list and /etc/apt/sources.list.d/mullvad.sources
  2. Uninstall Mullvad Browser: sudo apt purge mullvad-browser
  3. Open browser-choice and reinstall Mullvad Browser
  4. Run sudo apt install mullvad-vpn to install the VPN from the same repo the browser came from

item.title: Random log outs, amd_pstate failed to load, keyring mismatch, and more!
item.dc:creator: @sublime.dust
item.description:
I installed Kicksecure on my desktop yesterday, and since then I have spent several hours attempting to debug it, with limited success.

I am at my wits end.

After my initial install, I was experiencing many of these problems (random logouts, amd_pstate failed to load, kanshi config not applied automatically) and then the terminal suddenly stopped working. When I tried to open Qterminal or use anything in the System Maintenance Panel that would normally launch the Qterminal, nothing happened.

I could not find any way to fix this or install another terminal emulator, so I reinstalled the system from scratch. My terminal is back, but there are several other problems.

I considered creating a separate post for each of these, but it seems likely that at least some of these issues are connected. I’m using the latest version of Kicksecure, based on Debian 13.6.

Overview of Problems:

  1. Logged out of computer at random intervals
  2. Kanshi config is not automatically applied upon startup
  3. amd_pstate failed to load
  4. sudo apt update: Error due to keyring mismatch
  5. systemd critical journal messages - nouveau, channel 16 killed

1. Logged out of computer at random intervals

At seemingly random intervals, I am logged out of the computer and end up on the black log in screen where it asks me to enter my username. When I log back in, all of my applications are closed and anything I didn’t save is gone. This has happened while I am actively using my computer, and it has happened twice while writing this post. This could be coincidental, but it only seems to happen when I have adjusted the scale of my display.

2. Kanshi config is not automatically applied upon startup

When I restart Kanshi the settings in my config file are applied, but I have to do that manually every single time I boot my computer. I tried to get around this by creating the file /etc/rc.local with the following contents and giving it execute permissions. This script is supposed to run on start up, but my display config settings are only applied if I execute the script manually.

#!/bin/sh

systemctl --user restart kanshi

exit 0

3. amd_pstate failed to load

Every time I boot my computer, before I enter the passphrase to decrypt my drive, it outputs:

[    5.447055] amd_pstate: failed to enable driver mode(3)

When I run lsmod it does not list amd_pstate. When I run modprobe, it outputs:

[user ~]% sudo modprobe amd_pstate
modprobe: FATAL: Module amd_pstate not found in directory /lib/modules/6.12.111+deb13-amd64
zsh: exit 1     sudo modprobe amd_pstate

I have already tried updating my BIOS, enabling CPPC in my BIOS settings, and adding the amd_pstate=active rameter to /etc/default/grub with the following line before running ‘sudo update-grub’ and rebooting my device.

GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT="quiet amd_pstate=active"

Do I even need amd_pstate, or can I just ignore this error for the rest of time?

4. sudo apt update: Error due to keyring mismatch

This is the newest error, and it prevents me from using sudo apt update. It started after I tried to install Mullvad VPN, following the instructions on their website. Here are the commands I entered:

sudo apt install curl
sudo curl -fsSLo /usr/share/keyrings/mullvad-keyring.asc https://repository.mullvad.net/deb/mullvad-keyring.asc
echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/mullvad-keyring.asc arch=$( dpkg --print-architecture )] https://repository.mullvad.net/deb/stable stable main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/mullvad.list
sudo apt update

When I run ‘sudo apt update’, it outputs

[user ~]% sudo apt update
Error: Conflicting values set for option Signed-By regarding source https://repository.mullvad.net/deb/stable/ stable: /usr/share/keyrings/mullvad-keyring.asc != /etc/apt/keyrings/mullvad-keyring.asc
Error: The list of sources could not be read.
zsh: exit 100   sudo apt update

I tried deleting /usr/share/keyrings/mullvad-keyring.asc and /etc/apt/keyrings/mullvad-keyring.asc and rerunning the above commands, but it did not solve the problem.

5. systemd critical journal messages - nouveau, channel 16 killed

When I run System Check, I get the following output

ERROR: systemd critical journal messages check result (current boot): Possible system issue detected. Some unusual entries were found in the kernel log. 

There is no need to panic. This is not a serious security issue. However, it may affect other system checks. These messages might indicate hardware or software problems. 

Detected messages: 
Sep 30 14:14:34 localhost kernel: nouveau 0000:2b:00.0: labwc[2314]: channel 16 killed!
Sep 30 15:12:18 localhost kernel: nouveau 0000:2b:00.0: labwc[9098]: channel 16 killed!
Sep 30 16:00:58 localhost kernel: nouveau 0000:2b:00.0: labwc[16315]: channel 16 killed!

If you know what you are doing, feel free to disable this check. Create a file /etc/systemcheck.d/50_user.conf and add: 
systemcheck_skip_functions+=" check_journal " 
INFO: Kicksecure is a research project. 
INFO: user-sysmaint-split: Absent 
INFO: user-sysmaint-split session detection result: USER Session. 
INFO: Full Disk Encryption (FDE): Enabled 
INFO: GRUB Bootloader Password: Absent 
INFO: Kicksecure Login Security Check (Colors) :
+----------+--------------------------------------+
| Users    | Password               GUI Autologin |
+----------+--------------------------------------+
| root     | Locked (Present)       Disabled      |
| user     | Absent                 Enabled       |
| sysmaint | Absent                 Disabled      |
+----------+--------------------------------------+
You can adjust these settings using "Manage Passwords" and "Manage GUI Autologin" in the System Maintenance Panel. 
INFO: Secure Boot: Enabled 
INFO: tirdad - TCP ISN CPU Information Leak Protection: Enabled 
INFO: Kicksecure APT Repository: Enabled. When the Kicksecure team releases TRIXIE updates, they will be AUTOMATICALLY installed (when you run apt-get dist-upgrade) along with updated packages from the Debian team. Please read Trust to understand the risk. If you want to change this, use: 
Start Menu -> System -> Derivative Repository 
WARNING: Debian Package Update Check Result: Could not check for software updates! (apt-get code: 100) 
Please manually check: 
(Open a terminal, Start Menu -> System -> Terminal.) 
upgrade-nonroot

Should I be concerned?

item.dc:creator: @arraybolt3
item.description:
Did you set up the VM according to the instructions at:

Kicksecure – 24 Sep 26

Kicksecure for KVM

Kicksecure for KVM

If not, you may want to recreate the VM following those instructions.

Did you make any other customizations to the VM’s graphics configuration, like changing to an emulated graphics card other than “virtio”? If so, undo those changes and see if that makes things better.

It’s theoretically possible SimpleX could be the culprit. What you might try is: clone the VM, uninstall SimpleX from the clone, then use the clone for everything but SimpleX, and use the original only for SimpleX. if the VM with SimpleX running crashes, and the one without SimpleX doesn’t crash, then you know that SimpleX is almost certainly at fault.

item.title: Qterminal Issues
item.dc:creator: @arraybolt3
item.description:
Brave Browser is based on Chromium, and the bug was introduced in Chromium, so yes, it is very likely the issue.

Keep in mind that every time you open Brave, it will (likely) re-create the bad fontconfig cache, and you’ll need to remove it again. If you find this too annoying, you can create empty /home/user/.cache/fontconfig and /home/user/.fontconfig directories, then use sudo chattr +i on both of them to prevent Brave (or anything else) from writing to them. (You’ll have to do this from sysmaint mode unless you removed user-sysmaint-split.) This will break the fontconfig cache, but in my experience this doesn’t result in any real issues. There might be a loss in performance when starting apps, but if there is, I haven’t noticed it.

item.title: Sandboxing - what are the best options?
item.dc:creator: @arraybolt3
item.description:
desi_fubu:

Be careful with GIMP since you can run code inside GIMP’s Script Fu, its usefull for running a bunch of commands to modify an image and add cool effects but is an attack vector.

I mean, it’s no more of an attack vector than any scripting language to my awareness. You can’t embed a script into a GIMP image, so I don’t think there’s much risk here unless one is installing untrusted GIMP plugins. Of course, malware could install malicious GIMP plugins, but malware could edit ~/.bashrc too, and that would be a much more useful target since it runs automatically so frequently.

item.title: Add or create a utility for setting up encrypted drives/volumes/disk images/whatnot
item.dc:creator: @arraybolt3
item.description:
desi_fubu:

privleap or gsudo-x wrapper for allowing LUKS in user mode a starting point?

That would be a bit scary. If you can attach arbitrary LUKS volumes to the system, you can attach arbitrary filesystems where the kernel will look at them. If you do that, you can potentially impersonate the name of a disk the system expects to mount automatically or at least allow to be mounted without admin permissions. If you can do that, you can throw arbitrary filesystem structures at the kernel and potentially exploit kernel bugs. I’m not 100% sure how a more involved frontend would work around all of those issues, but some of them I have ideas for (use FUSE to mount the filesystem itself, require the use of a very narrow range of disk names possibly).

desi_fubu:

Yet again zulucrypt had Serpent and luks doesn’t natively have support for that algo.

I think it does? https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/8/html/security_hardening/encrypting-block-devices-using-luks_security-hardening mentions Serpent being used with LUKS, and running cryptsetup benchmark on Kicksecure shows serpent-cbc and serpent-xts among the benchmarked algorithms.

item.title: New to this, trying to install Tor and VPN
item.dc:creator: @desi_fubu
item.description:
Sonic:

Not sure if I want persistent anything going on at any point in time.

How to run ISO Live Mode from RAM?

It’s untested, but try using rd.live.ram=1. This is the equivalent of toram in Dracut, the initramfs generator used by Kicksecure.

If that works, boot into sysmaint and append it to the grub-live entry. Then when you boot from your Kicksecure USB (ideally with no internal drive connected, if you want to be absolutely sure), establish a WiFi or wired connection first, then yank out the USB. At that point you’re fully in RAM with no media left to write anything to.

Again if it works it depends on how much RAM you have and what you’re running (RAM exhaustive apps), you should be fine for most tasks. But if you’re dealing with transferring files larger than your total RAM? Yeah, that’s not happening, it’ll just crash.

item.title: New to this, trying to install Tor and VPN
item.dc:creator: @desi_fubu
item.description:
Alright, lots to unpack here, but I saw this thread and figured I’d chime in with some details that might help as I see some unmentioned info that may be useful. Please do one topic per thread going forward

Sonic:

I was looking for a Tails alternative, to use with the same “amnesic” concept, in Live mode. From what I’ve read, Kicksecure also wipes ram at the end.

First things first Kicksecure isn’t Tails, but it does have a grub-live boot option that’s pretty close. That session runs entirely in RAM, just like Tails. One heads up though. If you mount any external drives, traces can still get left behind, so be careful there. Same risk applies to both Kicksecure and Tails in that regard.

As of right now, the only way to get a “Tails like” setup with Kicksecure is to first burn a bootable media (looks like you did that). You’ll then need a second USB or external SSD, then install it the same way you’d install Debian with the GUI installer onto an internal drive. Just point it at the other USB or external drive instead. Worth noting to my knowledge, Dracut doesn’t support a persistence.conf, as discussed here:

Running portable application located on external drive Support
You should look into trying to create a persistence.conf for a Kicksecure USB, this might get you more towards what you want. It should work but I would like to get some others take on it. Since it is debian based technically it should work I would think and has been an idea I would like to try. Here is a guide from Kali linux but still applies: Manpage for persistence.conf https://manpages.debian.org/testing/live-boot-doc/persistence.conf.5.en.html

Anyhow after installation, you’d want to make grub-live the default boot option, then lock down the bootloader with a grub password.

Kicksecure – 23 May 26

Set grub-live as Default in GRUB boot menu - grub-live - boot an existing Host...

Optional. | Add a Live Mode entry to the grub boot menu on your existing Debian host platform. Stop persistent malware. Read-only mode. Make all writes go to non-persistent storage (RAM) instead of the hard disk.

Kicksecure – 13 May 26

How to set a bootloader password - Protection against Physical Attacks

Select an option. | BIOS Password, Problematic Interfaces, Screen Lock, Virtual Consoles, Login Screen, Side Channel Attacks

When you install software on Tails, you need an admin password for that session, conceptually similar to Kicksecure’s sysmaint mode, though Kicksecure is definitely more locked down and restrictive. On Tails, apps get saved to a persistent partition that’s not in RAM, while the rest of the system is RAM-mounted. With Kicksecure, you install apps via sysmaint (basically like a Tails admin session) whenever you need to save settings or software, then switch back to Live Mode for normal use. If you install onto a USB with LUKS encryption, you get an extra layer of protection on top.

Maybe full support for it will come down the road. More distros are moving toward Dracut anyway (Fedora already uses it). For what it’s worth, Tails itself uses this approach (persistence.conf), and Kali’s docs actually recommend it for setting up custom live USBs, which is pretty close to what you’re trying to do with Kicksecure. But again I haven’t found anything latest on any mailing list about it. Just thought I would mention it so you understand its not available yet but may change in the future.

item.description: I suspect that page is out of date. Simply upgrading the the Qubes kernel and rebooting dom0 is enough in my experience. The linux-image-* and linux-headers-* packages installed in the VM will have no effect unless you’re using an in-VM kernel, which is not (yet) supported.
